description: Compare your current mortgage with a refinance offer — monthly savings, total interest on both, and the break-even point on closing costs.

faqs.a: Divide your total closing costs by the monthly payment savings. The result is the number of months you must keep the new loan before the refinance pays for itself.
faqs.q: How is the break-even point calculated?

faqs.a: This tool compares only principal and interest. Taxes, insurance and PMI are not included, so confirm with your lender whether those change with the refinance.
faqs.q: Does this include taxes and insurance?

faqs.a: Generally refinancing makes sense if you plan to stay past the break-even month and the new payment is lower. If the new payment is higher or the break-even is beyond your planned stay, it usually does not pay off.
faqs.q: When is refinancing a good idea?

title: Refinance Calculator
